subject: Question about May postpaid invoice & VAT offset
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@heliohealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Anders P. <anders.proc@heliohealth.com>, Helio Health Finance <finance@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-20 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Unexpected overage on May invoice (invoice #504)

Hi Rishi,

We received invoice #504 for the May billing period and our finance team spotted a ~28% overage compared to the usage we expected from the portal. The attached CSV is Helio's internal tracking; the invoice lists 1,142,300 tokens billed while our exported usage shows 864,912 tokens for the same dates. Can you explain the discrepancy and confirm whether any VAT offset or credit applies?

Also: we previously submitted our EU VAT certificate (attached) — are we being charged VAT twice?

We need a short write-up for our payment run on Friday.

Thanks,
Elena
Finance Operations
Helio Health
attachments: invoice_504_may2026.pdf, usage-export-2026-05-01_to_2026-05-18.csv, vat_certificate_helio_2024.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20 11:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on May invoice (invoice #504)

Hi Elena — thanks for flagging and for the attachments.

Short answer: we’ll investigate token aggregation windows and VAT tags immediately. Two quick notes:
- We sometimes bill a small number of internal retry tokens (up to ~1-2% in rare request patterns) which can explain minor deltas, but 28% is larger than that.
- VAT should not be double-applied if a valid VAT certificate was on file; I’ll confirm whether the certificate was attached to your active billing profile or to an older account.

I’ve looped in Vanessa from billing to pull the raw metering logs and Laura from finance operations in case we need to coordinate a credit. We’ll aim to have an initial reconciliation before your payment run Friday EOD.

— Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: (none)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21 08:34:00 +0200
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected overage on May invoice (invoice #504)

Rishi / Laura — forwarding Helio's files. I pulled the metering records for 2026-05-01 through 2026-05-18 and attached a summary (small CSV). Preliminary findings:
- Our raw token meter (server-side) shows 1,106,412 tokens logged for the account across all model variants in that window.
- The portal export they used appears to be filtered to the primary model only (gpt-xxL); it omits reranking/embedding calls from their analytics view. Those omissions explain ~180k tokens of the gap.
- The remaining ~61k tokens are traced to a retry loop in a production webhook that had an exponential backoff bug (fixed on 2026-05-10).
- VAT: their certificate was uploaded to an old billing profile (profile_id: bp-78) that did not propagate to the current postpaid contract.

Next steps I suggest: 1) provide Helio a reconciled CSV showing the breakdown by model and request type, 2) apply a one-time usage credit for the retry-induced tokens (~61,200 tokens), and 3) reissue invoice #504 net of that credit and corrected VAT handling.

I can scope and issue the credit once Laura confirms the credit approval.

attachments: metering-summary-helio-2026-05.csv

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Helio Health Finance <finance@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-22 14:10:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected overage on May invoice (invoice #504)

Thanks Vanessa — good investigatory work. Vanessa, approve the numbers and request a credit for the retry tokens as an operational goodwill adjustment. Finance will accept a credit request up to $2,500 without extra approvals for accounts under a year-old contract; Helio's monthly run rate falls well within that threshold.

Helio Finance — we will:
1) Apply a credit equivalent to 61,200 tokens (applied as a negative line item on a corrected invoice).
2) Reissue invoice #504 with VAT removed from the original line if the VAT certificate is validated against the active billing profile.
3) Share a reconciled usage-by-model CSV and a short explanation of the retry loop root cause.

ETA: corrected invoice and reconciliation by Monday 2026-05-24 COB. Please confirm the bank/payment run date so we can ensure Helio doesn't pay the original amount by accident.

— Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@heliohealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-24 16:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on May invoice (invoice #504)

Laura — thank you for the quick turnaround and clear plan. Our payment run is scheduled for 2026-05-26; please send the corrected invoice by EOD Monday so we can process the adjusted amount. The reconciliation CSV will be shared with our procurement and audit teams.

Appreciate the credit and the explanation — please also include the fixed request ID range for the retry loop so our engineers can cross-check logs.

Best,
Elena
Helio Health Finance

(system note) On 2026-05-24 18:45:00 +0200 Redwood issued credit: CREDIT-INV-504-61200 (61,200 tokens equivalent, $1,872.00), corrected invoice link: https://drive.redwood.com/helio/invoices/504/corrected - invoice PDF attached to account.
